reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that individual motor behavior can be captured through two complementary descriptors: velocity profiles and motion amplitudes. Velocity signatures are derived from time-series data and reflect internal consistency within an individual's movement patterns. Amplitude envelopes offer a physically interpretable measure of variability, independent of complex MDS projections. These are jointly modeled using LSTM networks trained on repeated oscillatory motions. The resulting generative model preserves both statistical properties and individual distinctiveness. This dual representation enables robust cognitive architectures that simulate human-like motion in mixed reality environments. Failure modes include overfitting in LSTM models and insufficient discriminability of amplitude descriptors under low-variance conditions.
